rule: A crossed bound is a failed leg, recorded in failed-legs.json and left failing; only Carl resets one. A leg that cannot be measured (a file not supplied, a code not run) is NOT RUN and says why. A leg marked REPORTED has no band and is never counted. Legs have a set (S the synthetic cluster under the sample's selection; R the real Hyades sample; none) and a group (geo: the membership and the convergent point; dist: the space speed and the distance); the verdict function below reads both. Amendments are recorded in this file's amendments array before the gate stream is run, with what was found and how; the committed form's verdict binds until Carl rules. A bound, an estimator choice or a constant below is never changed after a result of the gate stream is seen: an improvement enters only as a NEW leg whose thresholds are committed before its first run, and the failed leg stays on record. No published value is typed anywhere except from a source file or document already in the repository, with its citation; a published comparison that needs a value not in the repository is a NOT RUN leg with an exact fetch request in MOVING_CLUSTER_GATE.md. The moving-cluster distance is not presented as a result of the project under any verdict below A.

scope.built: a membership rule from proper motion, parallax window and radial velocity; a convergent point from proper-motion directions; the space speed from radial velocities; the moving-cluster parallax of each star and of the cluster, with a bootstrap interval; the comparison with 233's parallax distance (js/kernels/galactic/astrometry.js clusterParallax with the per-star zero point of js/kernels/galactic/zeropoint.js) on the same stars with the same weights; refusals. All of it on a spike branch that is never merged.

syntheticTruth.note: Every number in this block is a synthetic truth chosen here for the test, labelled as such. None is a published value, none is tuned to any result, and none is claimed to describe the Hyades or any real cluster. The cluster's sky position is the query's cone centre (query.adql); the rest are round design choices that put the synthetic cluster's proper motion inside the query's proper-motion box.

cluster.unitPosition: pc per axis, isotropic Gaussian about the centre
cluster.unitSpeed: km/s, the space velocity of the cluster along the convergent point
cluster.unitInternal: km/s per axis, isotropic Gaussian, added to each star's velocity

errors.properMotionSigma: equal to the star's parallax sigma, in mas/yr, independent draws, correlations zero

radialVelocitySigma.unit: km/s; a star with sigma above 3 km/s is treated as having no radial velocity by the contract

zeroPoint.use: added to each star's observed parallax; the pipeline is given each star's zero point exactly (its own removal is 233's, validated there)

errors.note: the error scales are of the order of the first rows of the file (seen), not fitted to it

field.stat: stars that pass the sample's selection (parallax 12 to 40 mas, parallax over error above 10, the proper-motion box, the 25 degree cone) after errors, generated until 4500 pass
field.space: uniform space density inside the cone between parallaxes 12 and 40 mas

syntheticTruth.selection: every synthetic star, cluster or field, is cut by the file's own query (parallax 12 to 40 mas observed, parallax over error above 10, pmra 0 to 250, pmdec -150 to 50 mas/yr, inside the cone), so a cluster member the cut removes is not a member of the sample; the truth manifest records which survived

variants.E1: the cluster and the field above, 200 realizations
variants.E3: E1's construction with the radial velocities removed, 50 realizations
variants.E4: the cluster with 15 members (about 9 with a radial velocity), 100 realizations
variants.E5: the cluster with internal sigma 5 km/s per axis, 100 realizations
variants.E6: the cluster with an isotropic expansion of 0.05 km/s per pc added to each member's velocity about the centre, 100 realizations
variants.approaching: A3: the convergent point 130 degrees from the cluster centre along the baseline direction (the cluster approaches the Sun)
variants.perpendicular: A5: the convergent point 90 degrees from the cluster centre

syntheticTruth.truth: per realization: the member flags, each member's true parallax, the cluster velocity vector and its convergent point, and pi_true = the sum of w_i * true parallax_i over the stars the pipeline used for its distance and that are cluster members, divided by the sum of their w_i, with w_i = 1 / (parallax sigma_i)^2 (the estimand of the comparison below; a contaminant has no cluster truth and is counted by the purity leg)

constants.rvSigmaFloor: 1.0 km/s (sigma0, a stated floor for the intrinsic velocity scatter and the unmodelled radial-velocity error; not a published dispersion)
constants.rvErrorCut: 3.0 km/s (a star with a missing radial velocity or an error above this is treated as having none)

sample.cuts: astrometric_params_solved 31 or 95; ruwe below 1.4; finite parallax, proper motion and their errors; parallax_error above 0. No other cut: the file's own query is the sample's selection, stated through 154's selection object by the analysis
sample.geometry: n_i the unit vector of (ra, dec); east e_i = (-sin ra, cos ra, 0); north g_i = (-cos ra sin dec, -sin ra sin dec, cos dec); the sky proper motion p_i = pmra e_i + pmdec g_i in mas/yr, mu_i = |p_i|, t_i = p_i / mu_i; the great-circle normal b_i = n_i x t_i (a unit vector)

convergentPoint.estimator: c is the unit vector minimising the sum over members of (b_i . c)^2: the eigenvector of the sum of b_i b_i^T for the smallest eigenvalue (a 3 by 3 symmetric eigenproblem, unweighted: the pm direction error is a constant sigma_int / V for every star, because sin(theta) cancels, and the measurement part is far smaller). The sign: c is the convergent point, the direction the stars move towards, so the sign is chosen so that the sum over members of t_i . u_i is positive, u_i = (c - (c . n_i) n_i) / |c - (c . n_i) n_i|, the unit tangent at star i towards c
convergentPoint.derived: theta_i = acos(n_i . c) the angle of star i from the convergent point; off_i = asin(b_i . c) in degrees the star's offset from its great circle; mu_par_i = p_i . u_i the proper motion along the direction to c
convergentPoint.limits: the convergent point is two numbers on the sky; the assumed common velocity is an assumption, stated. A star with theta below 5.7 degrees (sin theta below 0.1) carries no distance.

speed.estimator: weighted least squares of the radial velocity on cos(theta_i) through the origin over the members with a usable radial velocity, weight 1 / (rv_error_i^2 + sigma0^2): V = sum(w v_i cos theta_i) / sum(w cos^2 theta_i); V must be positive
speed.limits: the fit has one parameter; if the mean of cos^2 theta over the used stars is below 0.05 the speed is not constrained ('perpendicular')

distance.perStar: pi_i = K mu_par_i / (V sin theta_i), in mas (mu_par in mas/yr, V in km/s); for a star with sin theta at least 0.1 and mu_par positive
distance.cluster: pi_MC = sum(w_i pi_i) / sum(w_i) over the used stars (members with a usable radial velocity or not: the speed needs the radial velocities, the per-star parallax does not; the used stars are the members with sin theta at least 0.1), w_i = 1 / parallax_error_i^2, the weights of 233's clusterParallax. The distance is 1 / pi_MC.
distance.interval: a bootstrap of the members (with replacement, the member set fixed, the convergent point and the speed refitted in each replicate, without clipping); B = 400 replicates per synthetic realization and 4000 for the real sample; sigma_MC is half the distance between the 15.865th and 84.135th percentiles of pi_MC (linear interpolation of the sorted replicates); the 95.45 percent interval is the 2.275th to 97.725th percentiles. A replicate with a non-positive speed or fewer than 5 stars is discarded; more than 5 percent discarded refuses ('unstable').

membership.stage0: the sample cuts above on all rows; the radial velocity is used only where present with error at most the cut
membership.seed: scaled coordinates x = (parallax / 2.0 mas, pmra / 20 mas/yr, pmdec / 20 mas/yr); the kernel density at each star f_i = sum_j exp(-|x_i - x_j|^2 / 2) over all sample stars; mean shift from the star of largest f_i (x <- sum_j K_j x_j / sum_j K_j with K_j = exp(-|x - x_j|^2 / 2)) until the step is below 1e-6 or 100 steps; the seed set is every star with |x_j - x*| at most 2. The seed is the only place a parallax scale enters before the iteration.
membership.iteration: from the seed set M_0, for k = 0, 1, ...: (1) fit c on M_k; (2) off_i for every sample star and sigma_off = 1.4826 times the median absolute deviation of off over M_k (floor 0.01 degrees); (3) V by the speed estimator over the members of M_k with a usable radial velocity, stopping with 'no-rv' when fewer than 10 have one (the radial-velocity and magnitude rules below are then not applied); (4) pi_i for every sample star with sin theta at least 0.1; q_i = pi_i / parallax_i (the observed parallax, so no zero-point code enters) and sigma_q = 1.4826 MAD of ln q over M_k (floor 1e-4). M_{k+1} is every sample star with: t_i . u_i positive; |off_i| at most min(3 sigma_off, 6 degrees); |parallax_i / median(parallax over M_k) - 1| at most 0.30; where V is defined and the star has a usable radial velocity, |v_i - V cos theta_i| at most 3 sqrt(rv_error_i^2 + sigma0^2); where V is defined, sin theta at least 0.1 and |ln q_i - median(ln q over M_k)| at most min(3 sigma_q, 0.25). Stop when M_{k+1} = M_k or after 30 steps ('no-convergence' if not converged, a refusal).
membership.centring: the magnitude rule is centred on the sample's own median of ln q, not on zero: it truncates scatter about the centre and does not select for agreement with the parallax scale
membership.members: the stars of the final M_k; the distance uses those with sin theta at least 0.1

refusals.noCluster: fewer than 20 members, or sigma_off above 3 degrees, or the robust scatter 1.4826 MAD of the members' radial-velocity residuals above 3 km/s, or fewer than 5 stars at any step ('no-cluster')
refusals.noRv: fewer than 10 members with a usable radial velocity: the convergent point is returned and the speed and the distance are null ('no-rv')
refusals.perpendicular: mean cos^2 theta of the used stars below 0.05: the convergent point is returned, the distance null

comparison.plx: 233's clusterParallax on the used stars: parallax, parallax_error and the per-star zero point of js/kernels/galactic/zeropoint.js (the synthetic stars carry theirs), systematic 0 (233 states a floor with its source or says it has none: none is stated here, the cap below carries the unmodelled), no clip. pi_plx the weighted mean, sigma_plx its statistical error.
comparison.tolerance: the leg agree passes when |pi_MC - pi_plx| <= 3 sqrt(sigma_MC^2 + sigma_plx^2) (consistent within the statistics) and |pi_MC - pi_plx| / pi_plx <= 0.03 (an accuracy cap of 3 percent of the parallax, so a wide interval cannot pass a poor method). The 3 percent and the factor 3 are stated choices committed here, not tuned and not published values.

oracle.what: tools/moving-cluster-oracle/oracle.py: numpy, scipy and astropy only, no Gravitas code, written from the contract above. It receives the sample (the real file by path; the synthetic realizations as pinned input files) and the per-star zero points as data, and recomputes the whole pipeline: seed, iteration, convergent point (numpy.linalg.eigh), speed, per-star and cluster parallax, and a bootstrap with its own generator (numpy default_rng, seed 234004). astropy is used for an independent coordinate check of the sky vectors (SkyCoord) and the Galactic frame, not for the estimator.
oracle.pinnedAs: oracle-results.json: the oracle's outputs, its versions, the sha256 of its inputs and of the script

amendments.change: the seed. The seed set is found by a count in convergent-point space instead of the density in (parallax, proper motion): the unit vectors c_k of a Fibonacci lattice of 20000 points (z_k = 1 - (2k + 1) / 20000, phi_k = k pi (3 - sqrt 5)); for each, the number of sample stars with |b_i . c_k| <= sin 1.5 degrees and t_i . u_i(c_k) > 0; the lattice point with the largest count (the first on a tie) is refined up to 8 times by fitting c to the counted stars and recounting at the fitted c until the counted set repeats; the seed set is the counted set. The seed uses no parallax at all, so no parallax scale enters before the iteration (the contract's iteration still uses the parallax window and the centred magnitude rule). The iteration is unchanged.

The AMENDED form adds AM1 to AM3 below and is a proposal for Carl to ratify: its verdict is reported beside the committed one and binds only if Carl ratifies it. design.stream: moving-cluster-234-design, synthetic data only, run before the gate stream and never on the real file: 3 noise-free clusters (and 2 each at 90 and 130 degrees), and 10 realizations each of the baseline, field only, no radial velocities, 15 members and internal sigma 5 km/s; 40 field-free baseline clusters for the diagnostic below. No gate seed (234001 to 234004) had been run.
findings: F1. The committed seed (mean shift of the kernel density in parallax and proper motion) found a clump of the synthetic field and not the cluster: on the first baseline design realization the iteration ran 30 steps without converging, 139 degrees from the true convergent point. The cluster's proper motions are spread over tens of mas/yr by perspective, so it is not the densest clump in that space. A count in convergent-point space finds it (AM1): the same realization converged in 6 steps to 297 members at 0.35 degrees.

F2. With no radial velocities the committed iteration (which applies the magnitude rule only where a speed exists) drifts onto the field and does not converge (6 of 6). The magnitude rule is centred on the median of ln q, so the speed cancels from it and it can be applied without one (AM3): 6 of 6 then return a convergent point at 0.3 to 0.7 degrees.

F3. A noise-free, zero-dispersion cluster is recovered exactly (convergent point to 1e-13 degrees, pi_MC equal to the truth), but 3 or 4 of its 300 members are not found: the contract's parallax window (30 percent about the median) excludes members on the near tail of a cluster whose depth is 10 percent (the committed analytic recall of 1.0 counted them). AM2 restates that recall over members inside the window.

F4. A bias of the plain eigenvector convergent point. On 40 field-free baseline design clusters the relative bias of pi_MC against the weighted true parallax is: true convergent point and true speed -0.05 percent (se 0.03); true convergent point, fitted speed -0.07 percent (se 0.04); fitted convergent point and fitted speed +1.29 percent (se 0.14, sd 0.88). The bias is from the convergent-point fit: the proper-motion direction noise (internal velocity scatter over V sin theta) enters the great-circle normals, and the least-squares criterion is weighted by sin^2 theta, which depends on c, so the minimum is pulled towards the cluster (smaller theta, larger pi). This is not amended: the committed estimator stands, legs C3 to C5 are expected to fail, and a corrected estimator may enter only as new legs with thresholds committed first (a question for Carl).
